items.name: HL · Customers from orders
items.what: Turns every order row into one row per real customer (phone normalised to +234, latest name, order count, lifetime value, first and last order, rank) with a single Code node, sending rows with no phone to a Fix list.
setup: Create one Google Sheet with tabs Orders (order_id, name, phone, total, date as YYYY-MM-DD), Fix list (order_id, name, phone, total, date) and Customers (phone, name, orders, lifetime_value, first_order, last_order, rank). Test data only.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential called "Google Sheets" and select it in Orders, Fix list and Customers.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all three Google Sheets nodes with your sheet's ID.
Orders has the lesson's 12 sample rows pinned (with fake phone numbers). Keep them for the first run; unpin Orders to read your own sheet.
When it works, replace the Manual Trigger with a nightly Schedule Trigger and publish.
items.test: Click Execute workflow with the pinned rows: IF sends 11 rows to Code and the Walk-in customer to Fix list; Code outputs 6 items ranked by lifetime_value, with Chef Tunde (+2348000000004) first on 164,000 from 3 orders and Mrs Adebayo merged into one customer with 3 orders and 73,500. The Customers sheet gets 6 rows; a second run updates them instead of adding more.

walk.title: Build it: one row per customer, ranked by value
walk.sample: 12 sample order rows · messy names and phone formats · one Walk-in with no phone

steps.say: We start with a Manual Trigger while we build. Later it becomes a nightly schedule.
Read every order from the Orders tab and pin the output, so each test uses the same twelve rows.
show: Google Sheets › Get Row(s) · Sheet: Orders

steps.say: Code that silently skips data is a trap. So an IF in front checks for a phone number first.
Rows with no phone go to the Fix list, so nothing disappears without a trace.
One Code node replaces about ten. We compare items with each other, so the mode is Run Once for All Items.
show: Mode: Run Once for All Items

steps.say: First, one phone format for everyone. Keep the digits, then turn a leading zero or two three four into plus two three four. Otherwise one customer looks like three.
Then group by the clean phone, counting orders and adding totals. Totals can arrive as text, so we convert each one to a number first.
ISO dates compare correctly as text, so first and last order need no library. The latest order also gives us the latest name.
Finally, sort by value, add a rank, and return a list of objects, each wrapped in json. That return shape is the one rule the Code node is strict about.
Save to Customers with Append or Update, matching on phone, so tomorrow's run updates the same rows.
show: Google Sheets › Append or Update Row

steps.say: Now the top ten customers is simply the first ten by rank, and every later workflow, including the agents in Track 4, can read this sheet.

walk.end: Execute it with the twelve pinned rows and check you get six customers, Chef Tunde first, and one Walk-in row on the Fix list.
